analysis:
Examined both source excerpts, the test patch and BASE source, and file metadata. TensorParallelCheck.swift adds documentation at HEAD 25–26 and a local CLI dispatch to GemmaCheck.run at HEAD 526–529. The dispatch follows row-routing initialization (516–517), but returns before the ordinary run path's termination handling, native-memory cleanup registration and deadline (579–582). GemmaCheck's implementation is not supplied; whether it installs equivalent resource controls and bounds requests must be checked in integration, not reported as an observed missing control. No new remote entry point or production serving authorization is demonstrated here.
CapabilityCommandCheck.swift changes the expected Gemma modes from pipeline-only to pipeline plus tensorParallel (patch HEAD 185). Surrounding checks still bind adapter, model, profile, arithmetic policy and partitions and reject crossed configuration/manifest identities (BASE 176–207). This test does not itself enable serving or establish runtime qualification. Integration should reconcile the advertised mode with Gemma metadata, resident runtime admission, peer authentication/encryption, cancellation and qualification evidence, relevant to TB-007/TB-011, T-007, T-010, T-053, T-054 and T-056.
Reviewed surrounding benchmark request validation, workload agreement, explicitly unauthenticated sealed-bench labeling, report output and prefix-record invocation. These are unchanged in the complete range map; no supported regression in A-001/A-003 confidentiality or T-041 cache isolation follows from the supplied changes. Production cache, attestation, billing and privileged-helper controls are not changed in this scope. No finding qualifies on this evidence; Gemma implementation and capability-to-runtime interactions remain material coverage limits for the next pass.
